regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8%; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% is the headline; the quality check is less flattering. IIP overall at 6.7% — down from 8.8% — while core sector slipped to 5.4%, suggesting the capital goods surge (IIP CapG at 16.1%) is concentrated rather than broad-based. PMI composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile) holds up, but manufacturing PMI at 52.8 is drifting lower even as services at 54.5 recovers — a services-led growth story is inherently harder to sustain when global demand softens and the BOJ is tightening carry trades that fund EM tourism and remittance flows.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45%; Fuel 22.93%","signal_text":"CPI at 4.45% is the number the press will print; the number that matters is fuel inflation at 22.93% — a 95th-percentile print, up from 20.05% last month, with Brent having risen 4 of the last 5 months. Core CPI at 3.9% (28th percentile) tells you underlying demand is not overheating — the inflation problem is entirely imported and energy-driven. The inversion: RBI's inflation forecast just jumped to 5.1% from 4.6%, which means the MPC is now forecasting an overshoot of its own 4% target — yet repo sits at 5.25% with no hike signalled. If Brent stays above $105, the second-order effect is a widening CAD → INR depreciation → imported inflation feeding back into CPI with a 2-quarter lag, forcing the RBI's hand precisely when growth is moderating.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1%; CD 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% — a 630bps divergence — with the CD ratio at 81.4% (75th percentile). NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% from 10.6% signals that as banks tighten deposit competition, NBFCs are filling the gap through wholesale funding — a structurally more fragile channel. The last time India's CD ratio sustained above 80% while the RBI was on hold, the taper tantrum of 2013 forced emergency rate action within 12 months; today's FX reserve buffer is larger, but the fuel shock is simultaneously compressing the current account in a way 2013 did not.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25%","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% with RBI's own inflation forecast at 5.1% leaves a real rate of approximately 80bps — thin cover for an economy running a widening current account deficit with fuel at a decade high. RBI's GDP forecast at 6.7% (below the market's 7.8% print) suggests the central bank is more cautious on growth sustainability than the headline implies — which argues against cuts. The BOJ's 25bps hike to 1.0% and US 10Y at 5.0% (90th percentile) tighten the global rate corridor within which RBI operates; any INR weakness from carry unwind forces RBI to choose between defending the currency and supporting growth — it cannot do both.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1%; CU 77.4%","signal_text":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% — up from 75.6%, now at the 74th percentile — has crossed the threshold historically associated with fresh private capex announcements. IIP capital goods at 16.1% confirms the investment cycle is not merely budgetary; it is showing up in actual production data. The risk: if the CD ratio stays elevated and banks face funding pressure, the cost of project finance rises — capex IRRs that worked at 5.25% repo may not survive a 50bps tightening, and the pipeline of announced projects could stall at the financing stage rather than the demand stage.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST 199853; PV 16%","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 crore is a strong print, but it sits at only the 71st percentile — and the YTD figure at the 14th percentile flags that the base is uneven. PV sales at 16% YoY and two-wheeler at 19.7% suggest both urban and rural demand are holding — two-wheelers are the more reliable rural proxy, and 19.7% is not a distress number. Credit card growth at 2.3% YoY (down from 5.6%) is the quiet contradiction: discretionary spend on cards is decelerating even as vehicle sales surge, implying the consumption strength is concentrated in asset-linked purchases (vehicles, homes) rather than recurring spend — a pattern that tends to be more rate-sensitive and more vulnerable to a fuel-driven squeeze on disposable income.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (Mar 2026) vs deposit growth at 10.8% — a 350bps divergence widening for three consecutive months. CD ratio at 81.4% (down from 82.5% prior month but structurally elevated). NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY, signalling wholesale funding pressure as banks tighten retail deposit competition.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios >45% — they'll poach deposits from smaller peers. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities; margin compression and refinancing risk are acute. RBI will likely signal deposit-friendly measures (higher savings rates, CRR cuts) within 2-3 months. Position for a 50bps rate cut by Q3 2026 if deposit stress persists.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile historically precedes either RBI easing or a credit slowdown. The last time CD hit 82%+ (2022), RBI cut rates 250bps within 12 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capacity Utilisation Breaks Into Expansion Zone","data_text":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% (up from 75.6% prior month), now at 74th percentile — a level historically associated with fresh capex announcements. IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY, core sector growth at 5.4% YoY. PMI composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile), signalling sustained demand momentum across manufacturing and services.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, industrial machinery, and cement stocks. Public sector capex (railways, highways) is the primary driver; private capex will follow 2-3 quarters later. Expect order book visibility to improve for L&T, Bharat Heavy Electricals, and Siemens India. Infrastructure debt funds and PSU bonds are attractive — capex cycles typically run 18-24 months.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77%+ has preceded 3-year capex upcycles in 2003-05 and 2014-16. Current level is mid-cycle, not yet euphoric.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"Affluent Money Entering Via SIP Backdoor","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,297 Cr (Mar 2026, up from ₹31,961 Cr prior month, rising 2 consecutive months). SIP accounts at 100.18 Cr (82nd percentile). But SIP AUM at ₹18.62 Tr (93rd percentile, rising 2 consecutive months) — growing 40% faster than account growth. Average ticket size per SIP account now ₹18.6 Lakh, up from ₹16.4 Lakh six months ago.","implication":"This is late-cycle behaviour: affluent retail (HNI/UHNI) is entering via SIP to appear 'disciplined' while deploying large sums. Equity MF net inflows at ₹29,329 Cr (68th percentile). Expect volatility to spike when this cohort reverses. Reduce equity exposure in small/mid-cap funds; rotate to large-cap, dividend-paying stocks. Overweight defensive sectors (FMCG, pharma, utilities) — they'll outperform when affluent money exits.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP AUM at 93rd percentile with account growth at 82nd percentile is a rare divergence, last seen in late 2021 before the 2022 correction. Retail euphoria is peaking.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation At Decade High, CAD Risk Rising","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile, up from 20.05% prior month). Brent crude at $105.58/bbl (73rd percentile), WTI at $101.94/bbl (83rd percentile). Both have risen 4 of last 5 months. India's oil import bill (at current volumes) will exceed $120 Bn annualised if Brent stays >$105. CPI headline at 4.45% (41st percentile) is being dragged higher by fuel; core CPI at 3.9% (28th percentile) shows underlying demand is moderate.","implication":"Current Account Deficit will widen to 1.5-2% of GDP by Q4 2026 if oil stays elevated. RBI will defend INR more aggressively, raising real rates and capping rupee weakness. Avoid long INR positions; hedge oil exposure via crude futures or energy stocks. Overweight refiners (IOCL, BPCL) — they benefit from crude-product spreads. Underweight consumption-heavy sectors; margin compression is coming.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is a 10-year extreme. Last time it was this high (2022), RBI hiked rates 250bps and INR weakened 8% within 6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"US Rates Sticky, BOJ Tightening Breaks Carry","data_text":"US 10Y Treasury at 5.0% (90th percentile, up from 4.97% prior month, rising 4 of last 5 months). Fed funds at 3.63% (flat, 67th percentile). BOJ rate at 1.0% (86th percentile, up from 0.75%, a 25bps hike). ECB deposit rate at 2.25% (59th percentile). US core CPI at 2.45% (falling 2 consecutive months) — Fed has room to cut, but forward guidance remains hawkish.","implication":"BOJ's tightening is the canary: carry trades (JPY borrow, INR/EM invest) are unwinding. Expect INR volatility to spike 200-300bps in the next 2-3 months. FII flows will remain choppy; DII (₹58,502 Cr, 100th percentile) is the only bid. Reduce leverage in EM portfolios. Overweight USD-denominated assets and short INR via forwards. US equities (S&P 500 at 100th percentile) are pricing in a soft landing; any Fed pivot will trigger a 5-8% correction.","pct_10y":90,"pct_note":"US 10Y at 90th percentile with BOJ tightening is a regime shift. Last time this happened (2018), EM currencies fell 10-15% and equity flows reversed sharply.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakening Into Structural Headwind","data_text":"INR/USD at 96.15 (91st percentile, up from 95.99 prior month, rising 3 of last 5 months). FII equity net at ₹29,631 Cr (83rd percentile, up from -₹3,111.9 Cr prior month — a sharp reversal). But this is a one-month bounce; the 6-month trend shows FII outflows dominating. DII at ₹58,502 Cr (100th percentile) is masking FII weakness. India VIX at 13.17 (8th percentile) — complacency is extreme.","implication":"RBI will intervene to defend 96.50 levels, but reserves are finite. Expect INR to test 97.50 by Q2 2026 if oil stays elevated and FII flows remain negative. Importers should lock in forward rates now. Exporters (IT, pharma, textiles) will see margin expansion — overweight them. Avoid rupee-denominated debt; duration risk is rising. Position for a 100-150bps widening in USD/INR forwards.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"INR at 91st percentile weakness with VIX at 8th percentile (complacency) is a dangerous combination. Last time this occurred (2022), INR fell another 5% within 3 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Rents Soaring While Vacancy Rises — GCC Decoupling","data_text":"Bengaluru office rent at ₹163/sqft (95th percentile, up from ₹148 prior month, rising 2 of last 4 months). Mumbai office rent at ₹335/sqft (100th percentile). Yet office vacancy at 14.7% (43rd percentile, rising 3 of last 4 months). Office absorption at 48 Mn sqft (55th percentile). Nifty IT at 23,217 (74th percentile, flat for 6 months). This is a classic GCC (Global Capability Centre) vs traditional IT services divergence.","implication":"Global tech giants (Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Apple) are consolidating GCC footprints in Tier-1 cities and willing to pay premium rents for trophy assets. Traditional IT services (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) are shedding office space as they embrace hybrid work. Commercial RE is decoupling from the IT stock proxy. Overweight premium office REITs (Embassy, Mindspace) in Bengaluru/Mumbai; underweight secondary office markets. IT services stocks will underperform despite strong earnings — the real estate tailwind is gone. This explains why Nifty IT is flat despite 7.8% GDP growth.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Office rents at 95-100th percentile while vacancy rises is a 10-year anomaly. It signals structural shift in tenant mix, not broad-based demand. Last time this happened (2015-16), traditional IT services faced 3-year margin pressure.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP growth with a 22.93% fuel inflation print is not a comfortable combination — it is a growth-inflation scissors that leaves the RBI with no clean move. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% and IIP capital goods at 16.1% confirm the investment cycle is real, not statistical; but core sector at 5.4% (down from 6.0%) and manufacturing PMI drifting to 52.8 suggest the cycle's breadth is narrowing even as its headline holds. GST at ₹1,99,853 crore and two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY keep consumption from flashing red — but credit card growth at 2.3% (26th percentile) is the trapdoor: recurring discretionary spend is already compressing under fuel's weight. RBI's own inflation forecast revision to 5.1% from 4.6% is the most honest signal in today's data — the central bank is telling you it expects an overshoot, and the market has not priced what that means for the rate path.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

5.0% on the US 10Y — rising 4 of the last 5 months to a 90th-percentile yield — is the gravitational constant around which every EM asset is now orbiting. US GDP SAAR at 1.5% (down from 2.1%) with US core CPI falling to 2.45% gives the Fed room to cut, but forward guidance remains hawkish — a combination that keeps long rates elevated even as the short end softens. The BOJ's hike to 1.0% (86th percentile) is the structural break: Japanese institutional investors who funded global carry trades at near-zero cost now face a 100bps domestic rate — repatriation flows from this cohort have historically been disorderly, and the Nikkei at a 100th-percentile 63,923 is pricing none of that risk. China's composite PMI at 49.5 and GDP at 4.3% (down from 5.0%) removes the one engine that could have offset tighter DM financial conditions — the global macro setup is simultaneously tighter and slower than three months ago.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

₹58,502 crore of DII equity buying — a 100th-percentile monthly print — is the single largest domestic absorption on record, and it is doing the work that FII flows cannot sustain. SIP AUM at ₹18.62 trillion (93rd percentile) is growing 40% faster than SIP account additions, which means average ticket size per account has risen to ₹18.6 lakh from ₹16.4 lakh six months ago — affluent savers are increasing allocation, not just new savers entering. The structural risk: bank deposit growth at 10.8% against credit at 17.1% means the banking system is funding credit expansion by drawing down liquidity buffers, not by attracting new deposits — a dynamic that tightens systemic liquidity even as equity markets appear flush. India VIX at 13.17 (8th percentile) against US VIX at 17.71 (12th percentile) is a complacency gap that historically closes violently when the external shock arrives rather than gradually.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Bank Nifty at 56,292 (93rd percentile) is pricing a credit upcycle while the CD ratio at 81.4% and NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% are pricing a funding stress — these two cannot both be right for long. Nifty50 at 23,218 has been range-bound for six months (down from 23,914 in the recent sequence) while earnings expectations embed a growth trajectory that a fuel-driven margin squeeze and tighter global rates will test in Q2 results. On real estate, the GCC-versus-traditional-IT divergence in office markets is now showing up in REIT pricing: Embassy REIT at ₹369.92 is down sharply from ₹439.58, Mindspace at ₹345.06 from ₹498.78 — the market is discounting that Bengaluru rent at a 95th-percentile ₹163/sqft is a GCC micro-market story, not a broad office recovery. Home loan rates at 7.5% (32nd percentile, down from 8.75%) are supporting residential demand — disbursements at ₹2,59,000 crore confirm this — but any RBI tightening triggered by fuel inflation would reprice this channel within two quarters.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Ranked by probability × impact: first, Brent above $105 sustained for another month adds approximately $15 billion to India's annualised import bill — CAD widens 40bps, INR depreciates 2-3%, imported inflation feeds CPI with a 2-quarter lag, and RBI faces a forced tightening into a slowing growth cycle. Second, the BOJ hike to 1.0% accelerates yen carry unwind — every 10bps of BOJ tightening historically correlates with 1-2% EM currency depreciation as leveraged positions unwind; INR at a 91st-percentile 96.15 has limited buffer. Third, the CD ratio at 81.4% with NBFC credit at 14.9% growth creates the conditions for a macro-prudential response — risk-weight increases on unsecured and NBFC lending would compress credit growth faster than the market expects, hitting consumption and capex simultaneously. Fourth, India VIX at 13.17 against a global backdrop of US 10Y at 5.0% and BOJ tightening is a mispricing of tail risk — watch the US 10Y at 5.0% for any break above that level, which would be the single most important data point to track before next week's Fed communication.

"}
